claim: When two incompatible stimuli such as a face and an object are shown to the left and right eyes, respectively, one does not perceive a constant superimposition of the two but rather an alternation between face and object, even though the physical input is fixed.
source: when two incompatible stimuli such as a face and an object are shown to the left and right eyes, respectively, one does not perceive a constant superimposition of the two but rather an alternation between face and object, even though the physical input is fixed (Figure 1a).
evidence: This is a well-established phenomenon of binocular rivalry supported by scientific knowledge and illustrated in Figure 1a.

claim: The proportion of cells modulated by the reported percept increases along the visual hierarchy, with 20% of cells showing modulations in V1 compared to 90% of cells showing modulations in inferotemporal (IT) cortex.
source: the proportion of cells modulated by the reported percept increases along the visual hierarchy, with 20% of cells showing modulations in V1 (Leopold and Logothetis, 1996) compared to 90% of cells showing modulations in inferotemporal (IT) cortex (Sheinberg and Logothetis, 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies by Leopold and Logothetis (1996) and Sheinberg and Logothetis (1997).

claim: The human fusiform face area responds to reported perceptual switches during binocular rivalry.
source: Using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), Tong et al., 1998 found that the human fusiform face area responds to reported perceptual switches.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Tong et al., 1998.

claim: The activity of neurons in the human medial temporal lobe and frontal cortex is modulated by the reported percept during binocular rivalry.
source: Using single-unit recording, Gelbard-Sagiv et al., 2018 found that the activity of neurons in the human medial temporal lobe and frontal cortex is also modulated by the reported percept.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Gelbard-Sagiv et al., 2018.

claim: Many of the modulations observed in higher-level brain regions such as the frontal lobe disappeared when subjects did not actively report perceptual switches.
source: Many of the modulations observed in higher-level brain regions such as the frontal lobe disappeared when subjects did not actively report perceptual switches.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Frässle et al., 2014 in the preceding sentence.

claim: Pupil size correlates with arousal, surprise, attention, and other confounding factors.
source: First, pupil size is known to correlate with arousal, surprise, attention, and other confounding factors (Bradley et al., 2008; Hoeks and Levelt, 1993; Preuschoff et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bradley et al., 2008; Hoeks and Levelt, 1993; Preuschoff et al., 2011.

claim: Optokinetic nystagmus is still present in monkeys in which the conscious percept is diminished due to anesthesia with low doses of ketamine.
source: Moreover, optokinetic nystagmus is still present in monkeys in which the conscious percept is diminished due to anesthesia with low doses of ketamine (Leopold et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Leopold et al., 2002.

claim: The macaque face patch system constitutes an anatomically connected network of regions in IT cortex dedicated to face processing.
source: The macaque face patch system constitutes an anatomically connected network of regions in IT cortex dedicated to face processing (Chang and Tsao, 2017; Grimaldi et al., 2016; Hesse and Tsao, 2020; Tsao et al., 2006)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chang and Tsao, 2017; Grimaldi et al., 2016; Hesse and Tsao, 2020; Tsao et al., 2006.

claim: The functional hierarchy of the face patch network, with increasing view invariance as one moves anterior from ML to AM, can be explained by simple feedforward pooling mechanisms.
source: For example, the functional hierarchy of this network, with increasing view invariance as one moves anterior from ML to AM (Freiwald and Tsao, 2010), can be explained by simple feedforward pooling mechanisms (Leibo et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Freiwald and Tsao, 2010 and Leibo et al., 2017.

claim: The representation of facial identity by cells in face patches through projection onto specific preferred axes can be explained by feedforward mechanisms.
source: The representation of facial identity by cells in face patches through projection onto specific preferred axes can also be explained by feedforward mechanisms (Chang and Tsao, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Chang and Tsao, 2017.

claim: One explanation for binocular rivalry is that it arises as a consequence of predictive coding, reflecting a high-level prior that two objects cannot occupy the same space.
source: One explanation for binocular rivalry is that it arises as a consequence of such predictive coding, reflecting a high-level prior that two objects cannot occupy the same space (Hohwy et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Hohwy et al., 2008.

claim: The percept of face or object could be inferred from fixations with accuracies ranging from 86% to 98% across human subjects (average: 93%).
source: We were able to infer which image the subjects were consciously perceiving with accuracies ranging from 86% to 98% across subjects (average: 93%, Figure 1c).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from human subjects shown in Figure 1c.

claim: After balancing contrasts, median dominance durations were 7.2 s for faces and 7.2 s for objects across the two monkeys.
source: After balancing, median dominance durations were 7.2 s for faces and 7.2 s for objects across the two monkeys.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the monkey experiments.

claim: In human subjects, median dominance durations were 8 s for faces and 10 s for objects as estimated from fixation patterns, and 8.1 s for faces and 8.3 s for objects as estimated from reports.
source: Similarly, in human subjects, median dominance durations were 8 s for faces and 10 s for objects as estimated from fixation patterns, and 8.1 s for faces and 8.3 s for objects as estimated from reports.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from human subjects.

claim: In the binocular rivalry condition the response of both example cells was higher when the monkey perceived a face than when the monkey perceived an object.
source: Importantly, in the binocular rivalry condition the response of both cells was also higher when the monkey perceived a face (as inferred by its eye movement) than when the monkey perceived an object.
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: In face patch AM, 73% (153/210) of cells showed significant consistent modulation by the conscious percept.
source: In AM, a face patch that receives input from ML (Grimaldi et al., 2016) and is the highest patch in the face patch hierarchy within IT (Freiwald and Tsao, 2010), the percentage of significant consistent modulation increased to 73% (153/210)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from recordings in face patch AM.

claim: Decoding accuracy was 99% for the best session and 95% on average for the physical condition.
source: Decoding accuracy was 99% for the best session and 95% on average for the physical condition.
evidence: This claim is supported by decoding analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 4d.

claim: For the perceptual condition, decoding accuracy was 88% on the best session and 78% on average.
source: For the perceptual condition, decoding accuracy was 88% on the best session and 78% on average.
evidence: This claim is supported by decoding analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 4d.

claim: Response modulations for both physical and perceptual conditions start around 130 ms after saccade onset.
source: We observed response modulations for both physical and perceptual conditions starting around 130 ms after saccade onset (Figure 5a).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5a.

claim: In the physical condition, a saccade during an object epoch led to response suppression, while a saccade during a face epoch led to response increase.
source: In the physical condition, a saccade during an object epoch led to response suppression, while a saccade during a face epoch led to response increase.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5a.

claim: In the rivalry condition saccades led to response increase in both object and face epochs.
source: In striking contrast, in the rivalry condition saccades led to response increase in both object and face epochs.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5a.

claim: Responses in the rivalry condition were less bimodal and spanned a smaller range compared to the physical condition.
source: Computing histograms of responses averaged across neurons for individual saccades shows that responses in the rivalry condition were less bimodal and spanned a smaller range compared to the physical condition (Figure 5b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5b.

claim: The decoding accuracy for distinguishing trial types (A,B) vs. (A,C) was 74%.
source: Remarkably, the decoding accuracy for distinguishing the two trial types was 74% (Figure 6b).
evidence: This claim is supported by decoding analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: The decoding accuracy for distinguishing (A,B) vs. (A,C) from the same cell population was 88%.
source: For comparison, the decoding accuracy for distinguishing (A,B) vs. (A,C) from the same cell population was 88%.
evidence: This claim is supported by decoding analysis of experimental data.

claim: Cells strongly modulated by the dominant stimulus tend to be similarly modulated by the suppressed stimulus.
source: This suggests that cells strongly modulated by the dominant stimulus tend to be similarly modulated by the suppressed stimulus.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the positive correlation between dominant and suppressed stimulus modulation indices.

claim: There are not two separate populations of cells that encode conscious and unconscious stimuli.
source: Thus there are not two separate populations of cells that encode conscious and unconscious stimuli.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the positive correlation between dominant and suppressed stimulus modulation indices.

claim: The neural correlate of consciousness in IT does not reside in a subset of cells perfectly reflecting consciousness but rather in a population code.
source: In summary, our findings indicate that the neural correlate of consciousness in IT does not reside in a subset of cells perfectly reflecting consciousness but rather in a population code.
evidence: This claim is inferred from multiple findings: (i) modulation by the conscious percept is weaker than modulation by the physical stimulus, (ii) both consciously perceived and suppressed stimuli can be decoded from the same population, and (iii) modulation indices for consciously perceived and suppressed stimuli are correlated in single cells.

claim: Face patches ML and AM are modulated by conscious perception and do not merely encode the physical input.
source: First, we found that face patches ML and AM are modulated by conscious perception and do not merely encode the physical input.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that cells respond differently to perceived face vs. object even when physical input is constant.

claim: Activity modulations attributed to switches in conscious perception in IT cannot be explained simply by active report.
source: Thus activity modulations attributed to switches in conscious perception in IT cannot be explained simply by active report.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the finding that modulations occur even in a no-report paradigm where monkeys had never been trained to actively report their percept.

claim: Cells in face patches are modulated by the identity of both the consciously perceived stimulus and the suppressed stimulus, such that both stimuli can be read out from the same population using different linear decoders.
source: Second, we found that cells in face patches are modulated by the identity of both the consciously perceived stimulus and the suppressed stimulus, such that both stimuli can be read out from the same population using different linear decoders.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing successful decoding of both conscious and suppressed stimuli from the same population.

claim: The finding that cells encode both conscious and suppressed stimuli challenges the widely held notion that in IT cortex almost all neurons respond only to the consciously perceived stimulus.
source: This finding challenges the widely held notion that in IT cortex almost all neurons respond only to the consciously perceived stimulus.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental findings showing encoding of suppressed stimuli.

claim: The quantitative difference in proportions of perceptually modulated cells between this study and Sheinberg and Logothetis (1997) may be due to several factors including different recording sites, imperfect accuracy of the no-report paradigm, and differences in stimuli and analysis methods.
source: The quantitative difference may be due to several factors including different recording sites (Sheinberg and Logothetis recorded from both upper and lower banks of the superior temporal sulcus in a less specifically targeted manner), imperfect accuracy of the no-report paradigm, and differences in stimuli and analysis methods.
evidence: This claim is speculative reasoning about potential explanations for differences between studies.

claim: The new no-report paradigm makes studies of consciousness in monkeys more accessible by replacing the need to train the animal to signal its conscious percept with a simple task that only requires animals to follow a fixation spot.
source: Furthermore, this new paradigm makes studies of consciousness in monkeys more accessible, by replacing the need to train the animal to signal its conscious percept (which can be a laborious process) with a simple task that only requires animals to follow a fixation spot.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the practical advantages of the new paradigm.

claim: The average response modulation during the perceptual condition was weaker than during the physical condition.
source: Our results show that for cells that are modulated by conscious perception, the modulation is not 'all-or-none'. Instead, the average response modulation during the perceptual condition was weaker than during the physical condition (Figure 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: In the rivalry condition responses appeared unimodal, lying in between the two clusters for the physical condition.
source: Surprisingly, we found a dramatically different response profile on single trials between the perceptual and physical conditions (Figure 5). Although in the physical condition responses clustered into two groups, in the rivalry condition responses appeared unimodal, lying in between the two clusters for the physical condition.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Single cells are multiplexing the conscious percept and the veridical physical stimulus during single trials.
source: This suggests that single cells are multiplexing the conscious percept and the veridical physical stimulus during single trials.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that responses in rivalry condition lie between the two clusters for physical condition.

claim: The subconscious stimulus could be decoded from face patch activity.
source: To directly test this hypothesis, we presented more than one binocular rivalry stimulus, created from pairs of three images, and found that the subconscious stimulus could indeed by decoded from face patch activity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the decoding experiment shown in Figure 6.

claim: The same cells that were strongly modulated by the conscious percept also tended to be strongly modulated by the suppressed stimulus.
source: Moreover, the same cells that were strongly modulated by the conscious percept also tended to be strongly modulated by the suppressed stimulus, ruling out the existence of a subpopulation of cells in IT purely reflecting consciousness.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing positive correlation between dominant and suppressed stimulus modulation indices.

claim: These findings strongly suggest that rivalry is not fully resolved before IT.
source: These findings strongly suggest that rivalry is not fully resolved before IT.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the finding that suppressed stimuli can be decoded from IT activity.

claim: It remains an open question where and how the conscious percept is ultimately isolated from the suppressed stimulus to produce conscious awareness of the former and not the latter.
source: It remains an open question where and how the conscious percept is ultimately isolated from the suppressed stimulus to produce conscious awareness of the former and not the latter.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of current knowledge and future research directions.

claim: The result that the suppressed stimulus can be decoded rules out Model I in which cells exactly reflect the conscious percept.
source: Importantly, our result that the suppressed stimulus can be decoded rules out the cartoon picture of Model I.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental finding that suppressed stimuli can be decoded.

claim: The findings are compatible with both Models IIa and IIb.
source: Our findings are compatible with both Models IIa and IIb, and future experiments may be able to distinguish between the two.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental findings and theoretical considerations.

claim: The new no-report binocular rivalry paradigm has several advantages compared to previous approaches that attempted to isolate representations of the conscious percept.
source: Compared to previous approaches that attempted to isolate representations of the conscious percept, our new no-report binocular rivalry paradigm has several advantages.
evidence: This claim is supported by subsequent discussion of advantages over flash suppression and backward masking paradigms.

claim: For flash suppression, the physical input when the target is perceived is not identical to that when it is suppressed, and thus any modulation observed may be driven entirely externally.
source: For flash suppression, where a stimulus flashed in one eye suppresses the stimulus in the other eye, report is also not required (Tsuchiya and Koch, 2005; Wilke et al., 2003; Wolfe, 1984). However, in that case, the physical input when the target is perceived is not identical to that when it is suppressed, and thus any modulation observed may be driven entirely externally.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations and logical reasoning about the limitations of flash suppression.

claim: If a distractor stimulus is presented simultaneously with a preferred stimulus, the response can be reduced compared to when the preferred stimulus is presented alone, due to simple normalization mechanisms.
source: Indeed, it is known that if a distractor stimulus is presented simultaneously with a preferred stimulus, the response can be reduced compared to when the preferred stimulus is presented alone, due to simple normalization mechanisms (Bao and Tsao, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Bao and Tsao, 2018.

claim: Backward masking is more susceptible to modulations arising from bottom-up withdrawal of attention or low-level (e.g., retinal) noise, whereas in binocular rivalry perceptual switches appear to be internally generated.
source: Also, it is more susceptible to modulations arising from bottom-up withdrawal of attention or low-level (e.g., retinal) noise, whereas in binocular rivalry perceptual switches appear to be internally generated.
evidence: This claim is based on knowledge about the differences between backward masking and binocular rivalry paradigms.

claim: The fact that monkeys had to simultaneously perform a very challenging unrelated task of saccading to jumping fixation points should alleviate the concern about the 'bored monkey problem'.
source: It is methodologically very difficult to entirely remove this confound, but the fact that monkeys had to simultaneously perform a very challenging unrelated task of saccading to jumping fixation points should at least alleviate this concern.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental design.

claim: Brascamp et al., 2015 reported that fMRI responses to binocular rivalry switches in fronto-parietal regions disappear when the difference between the percepts is made so subtle that subjects cannot report it.
source: Brascamp et al., 2015 reported that fMRI responses to binocular rivalry switches in fronto-parietal regions disappear when the difference between the percepts is made so subtle that subjects cannot report it
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Brascamp et al., 2015.

claim: Zou et al., 2016 created rivalry stimuli from orthogonal gratings where the grating in one eye was flickered fast enough that it was perceived as uniform gray and only produced fMRI activations in early visual cortex.
source: Zou et al., 2016 created rivalry stimuli from orthogonal gratings where the grating in one eye was flickered fast enough that it was perceived as uniform gray and only produced fMRI activations in early visual cortex.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Zou et al., 2016.

claim: Xu et al., 2016 performed optical imaging in V1 while monkeys were anesthetized and found that during binocular rivalry activations clearly alternated in counter-phase between left eye and right eye dominance columns.
source: In another study consistent with competition in early visual cortex, Xu et al., 2016 performed optical imaging in V1 while monkeys were anesthetized. They found that during binocular rivalry activations clearly alternated in counter-phase between left eye and right eye dominance columns.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Xu et al., 2016.

claim: Competition occurring in V1 is not incompatible with the findings of this study, although the findings suggest that rivalry is unlikely to be fully resolved in early areas.
source: We note that competition occurring in V1 is not incompatible with our findings, although our findings suggest that rivalry is unlikely to be fully resolved in early areas, given our ability to decode the suppressed stimulus from cells in IT.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental findings showing decoding of suppressed stimuli in IT.

claim: Hemodynamic signals, as measured by fMRI or optical imaging, only indirectly reflect neural activity and have previously shown discrepancies with single-unit responses.
source: It should also be noted as a caveat that hemodynamic signals, as measured in the above studies by fMRI or optical imaging, only indirectly reflect neural activity and have previously shown discrepancies with single-unit responses (Leopold and Logothetis, 1996; Tong and Engel, 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Leopold and Logothetis, 1996 and Tong and Engel, 2001.

claim: The current study describes the representation of conscious and subconscious stimuli in IT cells in the most confound-free way to date.
source: Overall, to the best of our knowledge, the current study describes the representation of conscious and subconscious stimuli in IT cells in the most confound-free way to date.
evidence: This claim is based on comparison with previous studies and assessment of methodological advantages.

claim: A study conducted in parallel by Kapoor et al., 2020 found modulations by conscious percept in prefrontal cortex using a different no-report paradigm based on optokinetic nystagmus.
source: Our study complements a study conducted in parallel by Kapoor et al., 2020 that found modulations by conscious percept in prefrontal cortex using a different no-report paradigm based on optokinetic nystagmus.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Kapoor et al., 2020.

claim: The existence of two directly connected functional modules with a hierarchical relationship (ML and AM) that both encode the conscious percept opens the possibility for future studies to investigate how changes in conscious percept are coordinated across the brain.
source: The existence of two directly connected functional modules with a hierarchical relationship (ML and AM) that both encode the conscious percept of a particular type of object opens the possibility for future studies to investigate how changes in conscious percept are coordinated across the brain.
evidence: This claim is speculative about future research directions based on current findings.

claim: Most cells showed stronger responses to the physically presented face stimulus since recordings were from face patches.
source: Since we recorded from face patches, most cells showed stronger responses to the physically presented face stimulus.
evidence: This claim is based on experimental data and knowledge about face patch properties.

claim: In face patch AM, 2% (5/210) of cells showed significant inconsistent modulation by the conscious percept.
source: In AM, a face patch that receives input from ML (Grimaldi et al., 2016) and is the highest patch in the face patch hierarchy within IT (Freiwald and Tsao, 2010), the percentage of significant consistent modulation increased to 73% (153/210), with only 2% (5/210) showing significant inconsistent modulation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from recordings in face patch AM.

claim: Face patch AM receives input from ML.
source: In AM, a face patch that receives input from ML (Grimaldi et al., 2016)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Grimaldi et al., 2016.

claim: Face patch AM is the highest patch in the face patch hierarchy within IT.
source: In AM, a face patch that receives input from ML (Grimaldi et al., 2016) and is the highest patch in the face patch hierarchy within IT (Freiwald and Tsao, 2010)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Freiwald and Tsao, 2010.

claim: In one session using the Neuropixels probe, 81 cells were recorded simultaneously in face patch ML, of which 63 were face-selective.
source: In this session, we recorded 81 cells simultaneously, of which 63 were face-selective (Figure 4a).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Above chance decoding of the perceptual condition was found in all 12 sessions.
source: We found above chance decoding of the perceptual condition in all 12 sessions (in all but one session, responses were recorded in both ML and AM, and cells were pooled across the two patches).
evidence: This claim is supported by decoding analysis of experimental data.

claim: A total of 653 and 481 cells were recorded in monkey A and monkey O, respectively.
source: A total of 653 and 481 cells were recorded in monkey A and monkey O, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data describing the total recorded cell population.

claim: The median and 99% confidence interval of eye position jitter was 0.038° and 0.34°, respectively.
source: The median and 99% confidence interval of this jitter was 0.038° and 0.34°, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by measurement of eye tracking precision.

claim: Trials with mixed or piecemeal percepts cannot account for the difference in response distributions between physical and perceptual conditions under the reasonable assumption that percepts were similar in monkeys and humans.
source: We of course cannot be absolutely sure that monkeys do not experience mixed percepts significantly more often than humans. Yet, under the reasonable assumption that percepts were similar in the two species, trials with mixed or piecemeal percepts cannot account for the difference in response distributions between physical and perceptual conditions.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from simulations and comparison with human reports.

claim: The simulated distributions only became statistically indistinguishable from the observed binocular rivalry condition if 50–70% of trials were mixed percepts of half-face and half-body.
source: The simulated distributions only became statistically indistinguishable from the observed binocular rivalry condition if 50–70% of trials were mixed percepts of half-face and half-body.
evidence: This claim is supported by simulation analysis of the data.

claim: Every human subject reported that on most trials they did not perceive any mixture.
source: This is markedly inconsistent with reports from every human subject that on most trials they did not perceive any mixture.
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral reports from human subjects.
